source_text: In the mid-20th century, public health rationales for male circumcision emphasized prevention of urinary tract infections (UTIs), phimosis, and balanitis, with studies indicating a 10-fold reduction in UTIs among circumcised male infants in the first year of life compared to uncircumcised peers. [82]
